name: Yakkasaray
tagline: Tree-lined central streets and the best cafe cluster
description: The compact district south of Amir Timur Square is where most of Tashkent's specialty coffee, wine bars and design studios have landed. Streets around Shota Rustaveli and Oybek are shaded by plane trees, Soviet-era apartment blocks sit next to new builds, and three metro stations put the whole city in reach.
bestFor: Nomads who want cafes, coworking and metro access all within a walk.
pros: Densest specialty coffee and coworking scene
Very walkable and well shaded in summer
cons: Rents run high by Tashkent standards
Older Soviet blocks have unreliable hot water
Traffic and horn noise on the main avenues

name: Mirabad
tagline: Markets, embassies and the new Tashkent City towers
description: Mirabad runs southeast from the centre, mixing the busy Mirabad bazaar and its produce stalls with embassy streets, older courtyard blocks and the glass towers of the Tashkent City development on its northern edge. It is central, mixed-income and the easiest area for finding cheap local food.
bestFor: Nomads who want central location plus daily bazaar shopping at local prices.
pros: Excellent bazaar for cheap fresh food
Walking distance to the city centre
Wide range of rents in one district
cons: Busy roads and constant construction dust
Quality varies sharply street to street
Summer heat is brutal with little shade near the bazaar

name: Chilanzar
tagline: The big Soviet-planned district, cheap and well connected
description: Tashkent's largest residential district southwest of the centre was laid out in the 1960s as numbered kvartals of low-rise blocks separated by courtyards and poplars. Rents are among the lowest in the city, the Chilanzar metro line runs straight downtown, and every kvartal has its own shops and market.
bestFor: Budget nomads staying months who want the lowest rent with a direct metro line.
pros: Cheapest rents of the well-connected districts
Direct metro line to the centre
cons: Ageing Soviet blocks with dated fittings
Almost no cafes suitable for working
About 25 minutes from the centre by metro

name: Yunusabad
tagline: Newer apartments, malls and international schools
description: The northern district holds much of Tashkent's newer housing, including gated complexes with lifts and reliable utilities, along with the TV tower, Ecopark and several large malls. It attracts wealthier locals and diplomatic families, and rents reflect that, but the building quality is a clear step above the centre.
bestFor: Nomads who want a reliable modern apartment and will trade centrality for it.
cons: Car-dependent, distances between blocks are long
Metro coverage is thinner than the south

name: Mirzo-Ulugbek
tagline: University campuses, green streets and moderate rents
description: The northeastern district is built around universities and research institutes, giving it wide green avenues, student cafes and a calmer pace than the centre. Housing is a mix of Soviet blocks and newer mid-rises, rents sit in the middle of the market, and Tashkent Botanical Garden borders its western edge.
bestFor: Nomads who want quiet, greenery and mid-range rents over central nightlife.
pros: Greenest large district in the city
Mid-range rents with decent building quality
cons: Long trips to the centre in traffic
Public transport means buses more than metro
